Title: Computer Systems Analysts
Task: Troubleshoot program and system malfunctions to restore normal functioning.
gpt5_rewards_justifications: LLMs excel at accelerating triage and diagnosis: quickly summarizing logs and traces, correlating alerts, proposing differential diagnoses, generating safe, annotated diagnostic commands/queries, consolidating fixes from internal runbooks and vendor docs, and drafting stakeholder updates and post-incident timelines. In steady state, this commonly saves 15–45 minutes per P2/P3 incident and 0.5–2 hours for complex P1s (roughly $25–$300 of analyst time at ~$50–$150/hr), and can reduce MTTR materially when used as a copilot while humans validate in staging or with dry runs, preserving quality.
gpt5_risks_types: Security, Privacy, Misinformation, Malicious actors and Misuse
gpt5_risks_justifications: Safety-critical: the wrong diagnosis or remediation can cause outages, data loss/corruption, weaken security posture (e.g., opening ports, disabling auth/logging), or violate SLAs and compliance. LLMs add risk via persuasive but incorrect root-cause analyses, version-agnostic or unsafe commands/configs, and hallucinated references. Capability-induced oversight risk is high during incidents: fluent, confident suggestions encourage copy/paste with less independent validation, especially under time pressure. Integrations that let the model run tools or access tickets/logs introduce new attack surfaces: prompt-injection through logs/KB pages or crafted tickets; data exfiltration of secrets/PII/IP to third-party services; and misconfiguration of automation. Compared to human-only troubleshooting, LLM+expert use raises the chance that hasty or unsafe fixes get applied (e.g., disabling security controls, running destructive commands) under time pressure; environment- or version-specific caveats are overlooked; injected content in logs/KB pages steers the model; and operators reduce peer review or rollback planning because the model’s suggestions seem authoritative. Many failures are catchable if teams enforce read-only defaults for production, sandbox/dry-run commands, RBAC and change management approvals; staged rollouts with automated tests and canarying; mandatory peer review; environment scoping and dry-run execution; source-linked responses to official vendor docs; egress controls and secret redaction; strict RAG allowlists to mitigate prompt injection; and full audit trails with easy rollback. With these in place, most model-induced errors are catchable, but under high-severity pressure oversight erosion remains plausible. Relative to human-only workflows, LLM+expert use can increase the probability of an unsafe change escaping review by roughly 10–25% without strong controls; with robust guardrails, residual excess risk is approximately 0–5%.

Title: Computer Systems Analysts

gpt5_rewards_justifications: High reward if used as a copilot with guardrails: accelerate triage and root-cause hypotheses, retrieve and tailor KB/vendor-doc steps, parse logs, generate safe-by-default scripts with explicit comments, draft user comms, and translate instructions. With human review, command preview, least-privilege execution, and references to authoritative docs, typical savings are ~30–60% on common tickets (e.g., 10–20 minutes on a 20–35 minute issue) and ~10–25% on complex cases via faster evidence organization, reducing costs $10–$60 per ticket at typical labor rates while maintaining expert-level quality.
gpt5_risks_types: Security, Privacy, Misinformation, Malicious actors and Misuse, Toxicity
gpt5_risks_justifications: Safety-critical: incorrect troubleshooting or remediation steps can cause outages, data loss, privilege escalation, or introduce vulnerabilities. LLMs increase risk via plausible but wrong or outdated fixes, hallucinated commands, and insecure recommendations (e.g., disabling security controls, broad chmods, unsafe registry edits). Capability-induced oversight risk is material: fluent step-by-step answers and shell/PowerShell snippets make analysts and end-users more likely to execute commands verbatim and skip safeguards (e.g., backups, staging, change management). Subtle errors in flags, paths, or registry keys can cause outages, data loss, or security gaps that are hard to attribute post hoc. Privacy risks arise when staff paste logs, configs, or credentials into non-compliant tools; security risks include prompt injection from logs/web pages, supply-chain/copilot code suggestions embedding vulnerabilities, and agentic tooling that runs commands or alters policies without sandboxing or approvals. Misuse vectors include attackers crafting tickets or prompts to elicit insecure steps or to exfiltrate info. Toxic replies are rare but possible in user-facing chat triage.

Title: Computer Systems Analysts

With a human expert leading and validating, most issues are catchable, but the high polish of current LLM outputs can create capability-induced oversight risk (analysts over-trust ‘complete’ SRS/user stories), making some failures harder to detect. Net: risk rises from low–moderate (human-only) to moderate (LLM+human). If an unsupervised, client-facing agent gathers requirements or browses external links, risk can approach high (≈4).

Title: Computer Systems Analysts

Feeding logs/dumps to external models can expose secrets or PII; untrusted logs can carry prompt-injection that steers agents or tool use; and highly capable models can induce overreliance, reducing depth of human review. gpt5_rewards_justifications: Moderate rewards when LLMs assist but do not decide: draft incident summaries with explicit evidence links, map observed behaviors to relevant policy sections, suggest clarifying questions and root-cause hypotheses, generate consistent and empathetic counseling scripts tailored to role/locale, and prepare follow-up emails and remediation checklists. Typical savings are 15–45 minutes per routine violation review and coaching conversation (about $20–$90 at $80–$120/hr), occasionally more in high-volume environments, while maintaining quality if analysts verify all facts against authoritative logs/tickets, require source citations, and keep final determinations and disciplinary language human-authored.
gpt5_risks_types: Misinformation, Privacy, Security, Discrimination, Toxicity, Malicious actors and Misuse
gpt5_risks_justifications: The task is safety-critical: incorrect findings or poorly framed counseling can enable repeat violations, wrongful discipline, or retaliation, and expose the organization to breaches, regulatory penalties, or litigation. LLMs increase risk versus human-only review by: (a) producing confident but incorrect incident summaries or policy mappings that induce automation bias and reduce independent verification; (b) omitting subtle context (e.g ., threat model nuances, business exceptions, or disability-related accommodations) that a human analyst would weigh; (c) privacy leakage if case artifacts with PII/PHI or credentials are sent to non-compliant tools; (d) prompt injection/data poisoning from attacker-controlled inputs (tickets, emails, headers, logs) that steer outputs; (e) biased or escalatory tone in counseling that could be discriminatory or provoke noncooperation; (f) outdated or subtly incorrect control or tooling recommendations; (g) capability-induced oversight risk—fluent, policy-citing outputs can induce deference and reduce independent checks; (h) adversarial manipulation/social-engineering via model-optimized appeals or poisoned artifacts; (i) legal/compliance exposure from inaccurate policy interpretations or accusatory language in counseling notes. Compared to human-only review, unsafeguarded LLM+human workflows can increase the likelihood of material error by roughly 50–200% on complex/edge cases; with strict controls (evidence traceability to primary artifacts, policy grounding with section citations, PII/secret redaction, model isolation from attacker-controlled inputs, and mandatory human sign-off), residual risk increase can be kept to roughly 10–25%.

gpt5_risks_justifications: Safety‑critical: flawed security policies, IR/BC/DR runbooks, and test plans can enable breaches, extend outages, or cause compliance failures. Privacy/Security risks include exposure of sensitive architectures and vulnerabilities to external providers, model memory leakage, and prompt‑injection via ingested artifacts; agentic tools could propagate insecure configs. Misuse risk if drafts leak and aid attackers. Compared to human‑only drafting with peer review, LLM+expert use without strict guardrails can raise the chance of a material omission or insecure instruction escaping review by ~20–50%; with private deployment, checklists, and second‑party review/red‑teaming, residual increase can be kept <10%.

Title: Information Security Analysts

Guardrails needed: no autonomous changes to IAM/DLP/EDR, enforce read-only credentials, zero-trust isolation, input/log sanitization against prompt injection, data minimization/redaction (or on-prem models), comprehensive audit trails, and mandatory human review/approval for any access-rights change.
gpt5_risks_types: Security, Privacy, Misinformation, Mal icious actors and Misuse
gpt5_risks_justifications: The task is safety critical: incorrect monitoring or access decisions can enable data breaches, compliance violations, operational disruption, and legal/reputational harm. Relative to human-only workflows, net risk increases modestly with strong controls (read-only access, mandatory human approval, provenance checks)—roughly a small but nontrivial increase—yet can be large (2–5x higher chance of harmful errors) if the agent has autonomous or write privileges or if prompts/inputs are not sanitized.

Using proprietary or regulated data without proper controls can cause retention or exfiltration of secrets/PHI. Dual-use: guidance can be steered toward exploit development, malware optimization, or bypass techniques. While disciplined processes (peer review, unit/property tests, fuzzing, formal methods, SAST/DAST, reproducible benchmarking) catch many issues, some vulnerabilities and correctness/performance regressions may remain undetected without deep verification (property-based tests, fuzzing at scale, formal specs, hardware-in-the-loop, red-teaming), particularly in concurrent, distributed, real-time, or hardware-accelerated contexts. Using LLMs alongside experts increases risk versus human-only workflows because current models often produce plausible but incorrect specifications, HDL/RTL, kernel/driver code, concurrency logic, or compiler transformations that pass basic tests yet harbor rare race conditions, memory-model violations, timing hazards, or microarchitectural side channels that are hard to detect. High capability can induce deference: well-structured code, convincing benchmarks, or citations can reduce independent verification diligence, especially in areas that are expensive to test (weak-memory concurrency, cache coherence protocols, speculative execution paths, interrupt/ exception handling), hardware–software co-design boundaries, timing closure, and side-channel resistance). Misuse risk is nontrivial: the same capabilities can accelerate exploit development, fuzzing, or microarchitectural attack design. Compared to expert-only workflows with code review, static/dynamic analysis, and formal methods, introducing LLM-authored artifacts without extra guardrails likely raises the probability that a latent critical defect ships by roughly 1.5–3x (about 50–200%). With strict provenance tagging, independent verification, red-teaming, and gated tool access, incremental risk can often be kept below ~20%.

Title: Computer and Information Research Scientists
Task: Develop and interpret organizational goals, policies, and procedures.
gpt5_rewards_justifications: High reward when LLMs are used for drafting and analysis, while humans own final judgments: generate first drafts, harmonize with standards (NIST/ISO/SOC2), perform gap analyses versus existing policies, produce control and RACI matrices, tailor summaries for stakeholders, and create training/FAQs. With authoritative-source retrieval and mandated legal/compliance review, typical time savings are ~30–50% of drafting/analysis effort on a policy initiative (e.g., 20–80 hours saved, ≈$2k–$16k at $100–$200/hr) while maintaining expert-level quality. Limits: jurisdictional nuance and organizational-specific constraints require human validation; benefits depend on disciplined governance (prompt hygiene, traceable citations, version control), and documented legal/compliance approvals; without these, rework and remediation can erase gains.
gpt5_risks_types: Misinformation, Privacy, Security, Discrimination, Malicious actors and Misuse
gpt5_risks_justifications: Safety-critical: Yes. Organizational goals, policies, and procedures drive compliance, security posture, research integrity, and workforce treatment; errors can create legal/regulatory violations, data breaches, biased practices, or strategic harm. LLM-specific risks: (1) Misinformation via confident but outdated or noncompliant clauses (e.g., misaligned with GDPR, HIPAA, NIST/ISO control mappings, union agreements), subtle omissions (breach notification timelines, approval authorities, DPIA triggers) that are hard to spot. (2) Privacy risks from leaking sensitive strategy/PII/IP in prompts or using non-compliant vendors. (3) Security risks from prompt injection/data exfiltration when summarizing external docs, or proposing insecure procedures that get codified. (4) Discrimination via biased policy language leading to disparate impact (e.g., monitoring, promotion criteria). (5) Misuse/attackers crafting adversarial inputs to sway drafts or introduce backdoored recommendations. Capability-induced oversight risk: polished, well-reasoned policy prose can induce deference, reducing thorough legal/compliance review. Compared with human-only drafting under standard review, naive LLM+human use can increase the probability of undetected policy defects by ~1.5–3x; robust mitigations (approved tooling, retrieval from authoritative sources, red-teaming, and mandatory legal/compliance sign-off) can bring residual risk near baseline.

Title: Computer and Information Research Scientists
Task: Develop performance standards, and evaluate work in light of established standards.
gpt5_rewards_justifications: Meaningful savings come from literature triage, drafting structured standards (scope, definitions, metrics, acceptance criteria), proposing checklists, generating templates, converting standards into test plans, coding baseline evaluators, and automating evidence collation. With expert verification, teams can cut 10–30 hours from a 100–200 hour standards effort (approximately $1,500–$9,000 at $150–$300/hr) and shorten review cycles, while maintaining quality. Gains drop for novel or safety-critical domains where rigorous peer review, piloting, and red-teaming dominate total effort.
gpt5_risks_types: Misinformation, Privacy, Security, Discrimination, Malicious actors and Misuse
gpt5_risks_justifications: The task can be safety-critical in contexts where standards guide security-, safety-, or compliance-sensitive research (e.g., evaluating AI systems, cryptographic protocols, or infrastructure-grade software). LLMs can produce polished but flawed standards, overlook edge cases, or embed biased/unclear metrics; they may also normalize data leakage (training–test contamination) or poor statistical practice, leading to misleading evaluations adopted at scale. Capability-induced oversight risk is material: because outputs look rigorous (formal language, citations), experts may defer and skip deep methodological checks, allowing subtle errors (leakage, Goodhart-able metrics, invalid significance tests, unrepresentative benchmarks) to persist. Privacy/security risks arise if proprietary datasets, logs, or PHI are shared with non-compliant LLM tools, or if agentic tools are prompt-injected via external documents, causing exfiltration or standard tampering. Discrimination risk stems from standards that underrepresent certain populations or contexts, causing systematically worse evaluations or thresholds. Misuse risk includes adversaries gaming LLM-authored standards or exploiting publicly shared evaluation code with embedded vulnerabilities.

Title: Computer and Information Research Scientists
Task: Maintain network hardware and software, direct network security measures, and monitor networks to ensure availability to system users.
gpt5_rewards_justifications: High reward when constrained to assistive roles: summarize noisy alerts, correlate events, draft incident timelines, generate vendor-specific CLI/API commands with dry-run outputs, create config diffs or Ansible/Terraform scaffolds, look up CVEs/RFC/vendor docs, and draft change plans/postmortems. With read-only access, sandbox validation, least-privilege tool bindings, and mandatory peer review, teams can reduce triage/diagnosis time by ~10–30% (e.g., 15–45 minutes per P1/P2 incident) and shave ~0.5–2 hours off routine change tickets and documentation, equating to roughly $5k–$30k annual labor savings per engineer at ~$80–$150/hr, while maintaining human-quality outcomes.
gpt5_risks_types: Security, Privacy, Misinformation, Malicious actors and Misuse
gpt5_risks_justifications: Safety-critical: network availability and security underpin business continuity and data protection. LLMs can produce plausible but unsafe configurations or commands (e.g., overly broad firewall/ACL rules, weak cipher suites, disabling verification or rate limits, mis-specified BGP/OSPF, brittle IDS/regex rules) that introduce latent vulnerabilities or outages; such errors are subtle and hard to detect in review. Integration with tickets/logs/monitoring increases exposure to prompt-injection and data poisoning from untrusted telemetry, leading agents to run dangerous actions. Use of production credentials/tools by agentic systems magnifies blast radius; leaked logs and configs may expose secrets or topology, creating privacy and security risks. High capability induces automation bias: well-reasoned remediation steps and runbooks can cause experts to defer and skip deep verification, especially under incident pressure, increasing risk versus human-only workflows.

Title: Computer and Information Research Scientists

In practice, managers can save roughly 2–6 hours/week (about $200–$900 at $100–$150/hr) by offloading first drafts, follow-up tracking, and status rollups, with quality maintained if outputs are reviewed before sending, sensitive data stays within enterprise-compliant instances, and decisions/resource allocations remain human-owned.
gpt5_risks_types: Misinformation, Privacy, Security, Malicious actors and Misuse, Discrimination

Compared to human-only workflows, LLM+human increases the likelihood of subtle coordination and information-handling failures unless strong approvals, data controls, and auditability are in place, and may reduce independent verification due to persuasive, well-structured outputs.

Relative to human‑only processes, unmitigated use likely increases error/bias and security incident likelihood roughly 1.3x–2x; with strong mitigations (structured rubrics, blinded first‑pass screens, adverse‑impact testing, mandatory human evidence traceability, PII minimization, secure deployment with contractual/governance controls, RAG on vetted policies, and injection/abuse red‑teaming), residual risk can approach but not undercut human‑only baselines due to remaining non‑determinism and leakage channels.

Title: Computer and Information Research Scientists
Task: Approve, prepare, monitor, and adjust operational budgets.
gpt5_rewards_justifications: High reward when the LLM supports but does not own the numbers: draft budget narratives and justifications aligned to policy, generate variance analyses and executive summaries, normalize and classify spend, build what-if scenarios and checklists from policy, draft SQL/Python queries to pull ledger data, and produce stakeholder-ready visuals and meeting notes. With calculations sourced from authoritative systems (ERP/spreadsheets) and traced back to line items, experts can maintain quality while reducing time by ~20–40% per cycle (approximately 2–8 hours saved on a 10–20 hour budget iteration), yielding roughly $200–$1,200 savings at $100–$150/hr, plus faster approvals. Prerequisites to keep quality: keep all arithmetic in audited tools, require numeric provenance to source line items and automated reconciliations, restrict model integrations to read-only data pulls (no writeback), use an enterprise deployment with data retention off and DLP/PII controls, enforce segregation of duties with mandatory human sign-off for material changes, harden against prompt/CSV/formula injection, and retain full logs and evidence for auditability.
gpt5_risks_types: Misinformation , Privacy, Security, Malicious actors and Misuse, Discrimination
gpt5_risks_justifications: The task is safety critical: budget errors can trigger regulatory noncompliance (e.g., misapplied indirect rates, unallowable charges on grants), audit findings, cash-flow issues, project cancellations, or reputational/legal harm. LLMs increase risk via confident but wrong calculations or categorizations (misstated headcount, CAPEX vs OPEX, fiscal-year cutovers, FX), persuasive narratives that mask omissions, and capability-induced oversight (humans defer to well-argued summaries and review less). Privacy and security risks are elevated because budgets include salaries, vendor terms, and confidential strategy; using noncompliant tools can leak data, and agentic workflows face prompt/CSV/formula injection and tool-API abuse. Misuse risks include staff/vendors crafting prompts or doctored inputs to steer allocations or justify spend, and scalable fraud or phishing. Discrimination risk arises if models generate biased rationales or heuristics that systematically underfund certain teams or demographics. Compared with expert-only workflows, LLM+expert can increase the probability that a material budgeting error escapes review by roughly 1.5–3x absent strict controls (e.g., from ~1–3% to ~3–7% per cycle), and substantially raises data-exposure risk if not run in a compliant environment; these failures can be subtle and hard to detect at scale.

Title: Computer Network Support Specialists

For new or replatformed setups, LLMs can save ~2–10 hours of engineering time via quicker script/policy scaffolding and documentation; for ongoing ops, ~10–30 minutes/week in log triage and change paperwork. gpt5_risks_types: Security, Privacy, Misinformation, Malicious actors and Misuse
gpt5_risks_justifications: Safety‑critical: backup integrity underpins business continuity, incident response, and compliance. LLM use raises risk by (a) misconfiguration or omissions that are hard to spot until a restore is needed (e.g., wrong paths/snapshots, missed systems, inadequate retention/versioning, untested encryption/keys, cross‑region gaps), (b) insecure suggestions (public buckets, weak/absent encryption, over‑broad IAM, hard‑coded secrets), (c) privacy leakage if production data, keys, or topology are shared with non‑compliant LLMs, and (d) agentic/control risks (prompt injection from logs or config files, unintended deletion/modification of backup sets). Capability‑induced oversight risk: fluent plans/scripts can appear authoritative, causing staff to defer and skip exhaustive verification/restores. Compared with human‑only workflows, residual risk can increase ~1.5–3x per change if organizations do not strengthen controls (peer review, immutable backups, mandatory test restores, least‑privilege, no external data to LLMs). With strong guardrails (on‑prem/compliant model, sandboxed generation, IaC reviews, automated restore tests), residual risk can approach parity (~1.0–1.2x), but remains non‑zero due to oversight bias.

Title: Computer Network Support Specialists

Under a change-management process with dry-runs, diffs, automated policy tests, and peer approval, typical savings are approximately 15–30% on routine permission changes (e.g., 10–30 minutes saved on 45–90 minute tasks) and 1–3 hours on larger policy scaffolding, partly offset by required verification. Net effect: material cycle-time and cost reduction while maintaining human-level quality only if every proposed change is independently validated before deployment.
gpt5_risks_types: Security, Privacy, Misinformation, Malicious actors and Misuse, Discrimination
gpt5_risks_justifications: Safety-critical: access-control and security-setting errors can expose data, enable privilege escalation, or disrupt business-critical systems, with legal/compliance impacts (e.g., HIPAA/PCI). LLM-specific risks: (1) Security—subtle misconfigurations (overbroad CIDRs, wildcard principals/resources, bad rule ordering, inherited group permissions, forgotten time-bounded exceptions) are hard to detect and can be confidently produced; agentic setups are vulnerable to prompt injection from tickets/wikis, tool misuse, and token exfiltration. (2) Privacy—sharing user lists, org charts, configs, or tickets with PHI/PII to non-compliant LLMs leaks sensitive data. (3) Misinformation—models conflate vendor semantics (AWS/Azure/Okta/AD), invent flags, or miss deprecations; fluent explanations increase acceptance of wrong changes. (4) Malicious misuse—attackers can craft change requests that steer the model or generate backdoored policies; LLM-assisted social engineering can bypass human caution. (5) Discrimination—if used to recommend access based on free-text role descriptions or historical patterns, biased suggestions may lead to unfair access gating. Capability-induced oversight risk is high: because frontier models often produce syntactically correct policies and persuasive reasoning, admins may skip exhaustive peer review or testing, allowing subtle but serious errors to ship. Compared to human-only workflows, using LLM+experts without strict guardrails can raise the likelihood of a harmful misconfiguration by multiples (e.g., 2–5x) due to silent, hard-to-spot failures; with strong controls (read-only generation, policy-as-code tests, mandatory peer review, dry-runs), residual risk can be brought closer to baseline but remains elevated from injection/handling risks.

Title: Computer Network Support Specialists

gpt5_risks_types: Security, Privacy, Misinformation, Malicious actors and Misuse
gpt5_risks_justifications: Safety-critical: incorrect or incomplete breach analysis and reporting can delay containment, trigger regulatory noncompliance, enable further compromise ..., and enable further compromise or data loss. LLM-specific risks include: misinformation (hallucinated IOCs, root causes, or timelines that appear plausible), security (prompt injection via hostile log artifacts, jailbreaks, tool misuse such as auto-running unsafe commands, and model/toolchain vulnerabilities), privacy (leaking regulated data when logs/PCAPs are sent to non-compliant services), and misuse (adversaries crafting telemetry to steer the model or exfiltrate secrets). Title: Computer Network Support Specialists
Task: Identify the causes of networking problems, using diagnostic testing software and equipment.
gpt5_rewards_justifications: High reward if kept decision-support-only. LLMs can rapidly normalize and summarize logs/pcaps, suggest differential diagnoses and next diagnostic commands, correlate events across systems, generate clear incident timelines, and draft updates. Typical savings: 20–40% on routine tickets (e.g., DHCP/DNS/VLAN misconfig, ACL issues) and 10–25% on complex multi-domain incidents via faster evidence triage; for 30–120 minute investigations this is ~10–40 minutes saved (≈$7–$53 at $40–$80/hr). Quality parity is achievable if experts validate all model claims against authoritative tools/runbooks and avoid granting the model change authority.
gpt5_risks_types: Security, Privacy, Misinformation, Malicious actors and Misuse
gpt5_risks_justifications: Safety-critical: incorrect diagnosis or unsafe remediation guidance can cause extended outages, data loss, or security exposure. LLMs heighten risk via (a) plausible but wrong root-cause narratives that induce automation bias and reduce independent verification; (b) misinterpretation of diagnostic outputs (e.g., ping/traceroute/pcap/syslog/SNMP) or omission of weak but critical signals; (c) prompt injection or data poisoning from untrusted device banners/logs and compromised endpoints; (d) leakage of credentials, network topology, or user identifiers in prompts; and (e) adversaries shaping incident context to steer the model. Relative to ...human-only workflows, incident risk rises primarily from automation bias and reduced depth of independent verification; in time-pressured outages this can increase the chance that an incorrect LLM-driven root cause survives to action from roughly 5–10% to 10–20% without guardrails. With strict mitigations (read-only tool access, injection-safe log parsing, redaction of secrets/topology, mandatory cross-checks against packet captures and device CLIs, and requirement to cite evidence for each hypothesis), the incremental risk can be held to low single digits. Detection is hard because failures are often subtle (e.g., spurious correlation of concurrent alerts, misattribution of loss to MTU vs. duplex mismatch, overlooking optical/link-layer errors hidden by higher-layer retries), and frontier models’ fluent diagnostics increase deference pressure.

Title: Computer Network Support Specialists

Using LLMs raises risk via: (1) misinformation/omission—confident but wrong device names/IPs, fabricated steps, missing timestamps or exceptions due to over-compression; (2) capability-induced oversight—highly fluent, well-structured summaries increase the chance that staff defer to the model and skip cross-checking raw logs/configs; (3) privacy/security—exposing sensitive network data, logs, and diagrams to external services (possible memorization/retention) and prompt-injection from log content; (4) misuse—insiders/attackers could generate plausible but falsified documentation to mask unauthorized changes. Compared to human-only workflows, risk typically increases by about 1.3x–2x without strong controls; with enterprise controls (no-retention deployments, redaction/DLP, required citations to source evidence, and mandatory human sign-off), residual risk can be kept close to human-only baselines (about 1.0–1.2x) while preserving traceability via required citations to logs/commands and attached diffs.

Title: Computer Network Support Specialists

gpt5_risks_types: Security, Privacy, Misinformation, Malicious actors and Misuse

Uploading configs/topologies to noncompliant services risks leaking IP schemas, device identifiers, and credentials. Because outputs look authoritative, specialists may shorten peer review or skip lab tests (capability-induced oversight), letting subtle issues (MTU blackholes, asymmetric routing, STP reconvergence, NAT/ACL shadowing, route redistribution mistakes) reach production.

LLM-specific risks include hallucinated or version-mismatched commands, insecure defaults (e.g., overly permissive rules, disabled protections), subtle ACL/NAT/order-of-operations errors, misinterpreting vendor- or OS-specific syntax, and suggesting untrusted package sources (supply-chain risk). Agentic setups with shell or API access expand the blast radius to environment-wide compromise via prompt-injection, credential exfiltration, and unintended command execution. Oversight risk is significant: authoritative-seeming, vendor-specific configs can induce deference and reduce independent verification, so subtle ACL/NAT/order-of-operations or interface-binding bugs may slip through and be discovered only under attack or during failover. Cross-vendor syntax drift (e.g., iptables vs nftables, ASA/FTD vs Palo Alto, Windows Defender Firewall vs pfSense, or cloud security groups) increases mismatch risk. Using third-party LLMs may also leak network diagrams, IP ranges, logs, or credentials if redaction and compliant processing are not enforced.

Risks can be reduced with read-only access, mandatory citation of raw metrics (utilization, loss, latency percentiles, error counters), dual-control for any change, allow-lists/dry-runs for commands, on-prem/VPC deployment with PII redaction, and independent verification in NMS/APM tools.

Because frontier LLM outputs look authoritative, technicians may copy–paste without full vendor-doc verification, increasing oversight risk versus human-only SOPs. gpt5_rewards_justifications: High reward when used as an assistant, not a decision-maker: generate stakeholder-specific question lists and risk/checklists, assemble RACI and acceptance criteria templates, summarize meetings with action items and open questions, build data maps and capability tables from source docs with citations, and highlight inconsistencies for follow-up. With enforced confirmation (stakeholder sign-off, traceability to sources), teams commonly save 1–4 hours per scoping cycle per engineer/PM (approximately $100–$600 at $100–$150/hr) while maintaining human-level quality.
gpt5_risks_types: Misinformation, Privacy, Security, Malicious actors and Misuse
gpt5_risks_justifications: This task is moderately safety critical: mis-stated system limits, data classifications, or compliance constraints during scoping can lead to costly rework, outages, or regulatory violations (e.g., PII handling, data residency). Using an LLM to draft questions or summarize stakeholder input raises risk via subtle omissions, overconfident or fabricated capabilities/constraints, and loss of nuance in summaries that may not be re-validated (capability-induced oversight/automation bias). Additional risks: leakage of confidential architecture or customer data if prompts/transcripts leave approved environments; prompt injection or tool abuse if the model ingests live docs/tickets; and persuasive but wrong trade-off analyses that sway teams. Compared with human-only processes, LLM+expert increases the chance that unverified errors enter requirements by roughly 10–30% unless teams require source-linked outputs and stakeholder read-backs; most failures are catchable with disciplined verification, but they can be hard to notice early.

Title: Software Developers
Task: Monitor functioning of equipment to ensure system operates in conformance with specifications.
gpt5_rewards_justifications: High reward when used as a copilot: natural-language querying of metrics/logs, alert deduplication, timeline building, correlation suggestions, runbook retrieval, and drafting incident updates/hand-offs. With human verification against source telemetry and gated actions, teams commonly reduce MTTA/MTTR by ~10–30% and save ~1–4 on-call hours per week per engineer (≈$100–$800 at $100–$200/hr) while maintaining human-level quality. Gains are largest in noisy alert environments and repetitive diagnostics; smaller for novel, complex outages where expert reasoning dominates.
gpt5_risks_types: Misinformation, Privacy, Security, Malicious actors and Misuse
gpt5_risks_justifications: Safety-critical: monitoring failures can cause outages, data loss, security incidents, or in certain domains (ICS/medical/automotive) physical harm. LLMs may miss or misclassify anomalies, hallucinate root causes, or propose unsafe remediations; their fluent explanations increase automation bias and reduce independent checks (capability-induced oversight risk). Logs and traces often contain secrets/PII; using non-compliant tools risks leakage. Log/prompt injection or adversarial telemetry can mislead the model or trigger harmful tool actions in agentic setups. Compared with human-only monitoring using mature dashboards/runbooks, introducing LLM-driven triage and diagnosis typically raises the chance of a missed critical alert or incorrect remediation by ~1.5x–3x unless strict guardrails and verification are applied; with autonomous changes, risk can rise ~3x–10x. If kept read-only for summarization with engineer verification, incremental risk is ~10–30%, but subtle missed correlations remain hard to detect.

Title: Software Developers
Task: Coordinate installation of software system.
gpt5_rewards_justifications: High rewards when constrained to planning and assistive roles: draft prerequisite checklists, environment matrices, and rollback plans; synthesize vendor docs; generate starter IaC/Docker/K8s manifests; convert commands across OS/shells; create validation tests; summarize logs and suggest fixes; draft change-management comms. With staging/dry-runs, peer review, and secret redaction or on-prem LLMs, teams can typically save 20–40% of coordination time on standard installs (about 2–8 hours, ~$200–$1,200 at $100–$150/hr) and 5–20 hours ($500–$3,000) on complex multi-service deployments, while maintaining human-expert quality.
gpt5_risks_types: Security, Privacy, Misinformation, Malicious actors and Misuse
gpt5_risks_justifications: Safety-critical: installation steps touch production systems, credentials, networking, and data. LLMs can hallucinate flags or steps, suggest insecure defaults (e.g., disabling TLS checks, broad IAM roles, open firewall ports), mis-handle version/OS differences, or produce fragile scripts whose errors surface only under load. Copying configs/logs into SaaS LLMs risks secret or PII exposure; agentic setups executing shell/API calls amplify blast radius and are vulnerable to prompt injection from docs, tickets, or READMEs. Highly capable LLMs produce authoritative runbooks that increase automation bias, so engineers may skip full peer review, staging tests, or rollback drills. Compared with human-only installs, using LLMs without strict guardrails plausibly increases the odds of a serious misconfiguration or security lapse by roughly 1.5–3× (e.g., raising a 0.5–1% incident probability per install to ~1–3%), mainly via subtle omissions that evade cursory checks.

Title: Software Developers
Task: Supervise the work of programmers, technologists and technicians and other engineering and scientific personnel.
gpt5_rewards_justifications: High reward when used as a copilot, not an autonomous supervisor: summarize PRs and diffs, generate review checklists and risk registers, draft test plans, triage CI failures/logs, surface dependency/license issues, auto-generate docs and meeting notes, and produce structured status rollups across repos. With humans retaining final approval and using defense-in-depth (peer review, comprehensive tests, SAST/DAST, SBOM/license checks, secrets scanning, and change-management gates), managers can cut supervision overhead by ~20–40% (e.g., 3–8 hours/week for an EM) while maintaining quality, accelerating cycle time, and improving traceability.
gpt5_risks_types: Misinformation, Privacy, Security, Malicious actors and Misuse, Discrimination, Toxicity
gpt5_risks_justifications: Safety-critical at the organizational level: supervision shapes code quality, security, reliability, compliance, and team well‑being. LLMs can produce confident but incorrect reviews, risk assessments, or compliance guidance; generate or approve changes that subtly degrade security or performance; and mis-summarize CI/log evidence. Capability-induced oversight risk is material: because frontier LLMs now give high-quality code explanations and diff analyses, supervisors may defer to them and reduce independent verification, letting subtle vulnerabilities or architectural missteps slip. Privacy risks arise when proprietary code, incident data, or employee PII are shared with non-compliant services. Security risks include prompt-injection from repository content (README/PR descriptions/tests), tool/agent misuse with repo or CI write access, leakage of secrets, license/compliance hallucinations, and weakened supply-chain hygiene. Misuse risks include employees gaming AI-driven evaluations or deepfaked activity summaries. Discrimination/toxicity risks occur if the model drafts biased performance feedback or toxic comments that harm inclusion. Compared to human-only supervision, lack of strong guardrails can increase the probability of accepting a materially flawed change or missing a key risk by ~20–60% for complex reviews; with autonomous repo actions the risk escalates (would rate 4) due to low-visibility, hard-to-detect failures.

Title: Software Developers

gpt5_risks_types: Misinformation, Security, Privacy, Malicious actors and Misuse, Discrimination
gpt5_risks_justifications: Safety-critical in many deployments: incorrect or incomplete training on enterprise or operational equipment can cause outages, data loss, insecure configurations, compliance violations, or (for connected/industrial or medical-adjacent gear) physical safety risks. LLMs raise risk via: (a) fluent but wrong steps, version/firmware generalization errors, or hallucinated commands that are hard to notice; (b) insecure advice (e.g., disabling MFA, opening broad firewall rules) that looks reasonable; (c) automation-bias/oversight risk—polished LLM drafts can lead SMEs to under-test instructions; (d) privacy leakage if user logs, screenshots, or device IDs are fed to non-compliant systems; (e) prompt-injection or poisoned manuals w/ hidden instructions that steer an LLM-based trainer to give harmful guidance; (f) subtle bias in examples or accessibility gaps disadvantaging certain user groups. Compared with human-only training, the likelihood that a consequential error slips into final materials or live demos increases moderately. Many issues are catchable with staged dry-runs on the exact software/firmware versions, principle-of-least-privilege defaults, and red-team reviews, but capability-induced oversight risk means polished LLM outputs can reduce diligence and shorten validation steps, letting environment-specific edge cases or insecure defaults slip through. Lightweight mitigations (redaction, injection-safe browsers, checklist-based verification) add only a few minutes, so net time/cost still decreases while maintaining expert-level quality.
gpt5_risks_types: Misinformation, Privacy, Security, Malicious actors and Misuse
gpt5_risks_justifications: This QA task is safety-critical at the organizational level: missed or mischaracterized defects can cause outages, security incidents, or compliance failures. Relative to human-only QA, naive deployment can raise missed-defect risk by approximately 20–50% in cases where analysts defer to the model; with guardrails (sanitized/redacted data, injection-resistant prompts/tools, evidence-linked checklists, and mandatory human repro), added risk can be constrained to approximately 5–10%.

Title: Web Developers
Task: Confer with management or development teams to prioritize needs, resolve conflicts, develop content criteria, or choose solutions.
gpt5_rewards_justifications: High reward on synthesis and communication: draft option trade-offs, decision memos, ADRs, meeting agendas, conflict-resolution proposals, acceptance criteria, risk registers, and stakeholder summaries; cluster and prioritize requirements; surface duplicates and dependencies; estimate effort ranges from historical data (to be validated). With expert verification using checklists and authoritative sources, typical savings are 2–6 hours per decision package (roughly 30–50% of a 6–12 hour effort), plus 0.5–2 hours per weekly prioritization cycle, equating to about $120–$960 per cycle at $60–$120/hr, while maintaining quality.
gpt5_risks_types: Misinformation, Privacy, Security, Discrimination, Malicious actors and Misuse
gpt5_risks_justifications: Safety-critical at the organizational level: prioritization and solution choices influence architecture, compliance, security posture, accessibility, and content policy. LLMs raise risk by (a) producing persuasive but incorrect trade‑off analyses, hallucinated references, or flawed cost/effort estimates; (b) capability‑induced oversight—teams may over‑defer to confident model proposals and miss subtle security (e.g., OWASP issues), licensing, or compliance pitfalls; (c) privacy exposure if internal roadmaps or user data are pasted into non‑compliant tools; (d) security risks from prompt-injection or delegated tool use if connected to issue trackers, repos, or RAG sources; recommending vulnerable packages or non-compliant licenses; and inadvertent leakage of internal roadmaps in shared AI workspaces; (e) discrimination/accessibility issues if content criteria or acceptance tests deprioritize a11y, localization, or underserved users; (f) misuse where actors seed AI inputs with adversarial or manipulative content to steer decisions. Many issues are catchable via independent threat, license, and cost reviews, but polished LLM analyses can induce deference and reduce depth of review, so some subtle strategic, legal, or security missteps may slip through.

Title: Web Developers
Task: Communicate with network personnel or Web site hosting agencies to address hardware or software issues affecting Web sites.
gpt5_rewards_justifications: High reward when the LLM is used for communication scaffolding rather than decision-making: draft clear, complete tickets; summarize and structure logs into timelines; generate targeted diagnostic questions; translate across languages/time zones; standardize formats for different providers; and draft post-incident follow-ups. With experts verifying technical claims and scrubbing sensitive data, typical savings are about 10–45 minutes per issue (approximately $20–$150 at $60–$120/hr), often reducing back-and-forth and accelerating resolution while keeping human quality controls.
gpt5_risks_types: Misinformation, Privacy, Security, Malicious actors and Misuse
gpt5_risks_justifications: Safety-critical at the organizational level: incorrect or overly authoritative LLM-drafted messages to hosting providers can trigger misconfigurations, outages, data loss, or delayed incident resolution. LLMs can confidently misstate root causes, omit key evidence, or propose unauthorized corrective actions; their fluent tone increases automation bias, so developers may copy‑paste without full verification under time pressure. Sharing raw logs or screenshots with an LLM can expose secrets or customer data; agentic setups risk prompt injection from untrusted logs/errors and could accidentally disclose credentials or request risky changes. Compared to human-only workflows, combined use modestly to moderately increases risk (roughly 1.2x–1.6x likelihood of harmful miscommunication or inadvertent disclosure) unless strict redaction, fact-checking against source telemetry, and approval gates for any requested provider action are enforced.

Title: Web Developers
Task: Collaborate with management or users to develop e-commerce strategies and to integrate these strategies with Web sites.
gpt5_rewards_justifications: Rewards are meaningful but require rigorous review to keep quality. LLMs can accelerate strategy drafts, competitive scans, KPI frameworks, customer journey maps, promo calendars, and turn stakeholder input into PRDs, user stories, and acceptance criteria; generate localized/SEO copy, email/ads, and support content; propose A/B tests and personalization rules; draft integration plans for platforms/gateways (e.g., Shopify, WooCommerce, Magento, Stripe, Adyen, PayPal), including webhook/event maps, error handling, and edge cases; scaffold snippets for carts/checkout/subscriptions/tax/shipping/inventory plus unit/integration tests; outline analytics schemas (GA4/Segment), tag plans, and consent flows; and produce migration checklists, runbooks, and stakeholder comms. With strict controls (vetted templates, dependency allowlists, RAG over internal standards, SAST/DAST/dependency scans, and mandatory security/compliance review), teams typically save 10–30 hours across discovery and integration planning, roughly $1,500–$6,000 at $75–$200/hr, yielding about 10–20% faster delivery for SMB/mid-market projects while maintaining expert quality.
gpt5_risks_types: Security, Privacy, Misinformation, Discrimination, Toxicity, Malicious actors and Misuse
gpt5_risks_justifications: Safety-critical: e-commerce strategy and integration touch payments, PII, and regulatory/compliance surfaces; errors can cause data breaches, fraud, legal penalties ( PCI DSS fines, GDPR/CCPA violations), revenue loss, or reputational damage. LLM-specific risks: (1) Security—generated code or architecture may embed OWASP-class flaws (e.g., auth/session misconfig, insecure payment gateway usage, SSRF, injection), include vulnerable/typosquatted packages, mishandle secrets, or be compromised by prompt-injection from CMS/product feeds or third-party plugins; agentic tools can be abused to exfiltrate data. (2) Privacy—models may memorize or leak customer data, draft policies that are non-compliant, or over-collect data through analytics tags. (3) Misinformation—confident but wrong guidance on tax, cross-border shipping, returns, accessibility, or cookie consent; persuasive copy may misstate claims, pricing, or availability. (4) Discrimination/Toxicity—personalization or ad targeting suggestions that disadvantage protected groups; copy that is culturally insensitive. (5) Misuse—attackers can leverage the same systems to craft phishing pages, refund-fraud playbooks, or SEO spam. Capability-induced oversight risk: high-quality plans and code snippets look authoritative, increasing deference and reducing depth of review, so subtle vulnerabilities or noncompliance can escape detection. While experts can catch many issues with code review, dependency scanning, and compliance checklists, these failures are often hard to detect reliably before production, justifying a high risk rating.

Title: Web Developers
Task: Document test plans, testing procedures, or test results.
gpt5_rewards_justifications: High reward on drafting and structuring: generate test plan templates, traceability matrices, procedure step lists, acceptance criteria mappings, and readable summaries of CI logs and flaky test patterns; normalize formats across teams; auto-link to cases and tickets; translate between audiences. With expert verification of scope, metrics, and pass/fail reasoning, teams often save 30–60% of documentation time (e.g., 1–4 hours per feature/release at $80–$150/hr, roughly $80–$600), while maintaining quality. Larger suites see minutes saved per run via automated result rollups and anomaly highlighting.
gpt5_risks_types: Misinformation, Privacy, Security, Malicious actors and Misuse
gpt5_risks_justifications: This task can be safety-critical at the organizational level: inaccurate test plans/procedures or mis-summarized results can let defects or security vulnerabilities ship, causing outages, data exposure, or compliance failures. LLMs increase risk by: (a) generating confident but wrong coverage claims, pass/fail statuses, or fabricated references to tests; (b) misinterpreting CI logs and flaky test output; (c) capability-induced oversight—polished docs make reviewers defer and skip independent checks; (d) privacy and security exposure when logs, stack traces, or datasets with secrets/PII are sent to external models; (e) prompt-injection via hostile logs or artifacts and unauthorized repo changes changes if connected tools have write permissions. Overall, many issues are catchable via peer review, CI status, and traceability checks, but the fluency of LLM prose can conceal gaps in coverage or misread logs unless reviewers independently verify against code, test artifacts, and requirements.

Title: Web Developers
Task: Establish appropriate server directory trees.
gpt5_rewards_justifications: LLMs can speed up producing framework-appropriate directory scaffolds, cross-OS creation/permission scripts, IaC/Ansible snippets, and security checklists, and can explain trade-offs (webroot vs private dirs, per-service users, least privilege). With expert verification and hardening, this typically saves 30–90 minutes per service or several hours across a fleet (about $50–$500 at $75–$ 150/hr), while keeping quality if they validate against CIS/NIST baselines, enforce least privilege (dedicated service users, 0640/0750, noexec/nodev on uploads/tmp), disable directory listing, and require peer review before production.
gpt5_risks_types: Security, Privacy, Misinformation, Malicious actors and Misuse
gpt5_risks_justifications: This task is safety critical because directory layout and permissions determine what is publicly reachable, writable, and isolated. LLMs can propose plausible but unsafe layouts (e.g., placing writable uploads or backups under the webroot, enabling directory listing, overly permissive modes/umask, exposing .git/.env/logs, weak user/group separation, unsafe symlinks, incorrect SELinux/AppArmor contexts, or missing noexec/nodev on tmp). If used as an agent with shell/tools, the model may execute risky commands or fetch untrusted scripts; prompt injection can steer it toward weaker protections. Failures can be subtle and pass casual review, and fluent explanations can induce deference (capability-induced oversight). Nonetheless, a competent engineer can usually catch issues with security baselines, peer review, and automated checks (linters/scanners), keeping residual risk moderate compared to human-only workflows.

Title: Web Developers
Task: Recommend and implement performance improvements.
gpt5_rewards_justifications: Substantial gains when used as an assistant with guardrails: triage Lighthouse/WebPageTest outputs; suggest targeted fixes (code-splitting, lazy loading, tree-shaking, image/font optimization, preconnect/preload, HTTP caching, CDN rules, compression/Brotli, bundler config); auto-generate profiling plans, trace interpretations, and PRs with tests; produce rollback plans and dashboards. With expert validation, CI checks, and perf budgets, teams commonly save 20–40% on audit and remediation time (about 5–30 engineer-hours on a typical app, ~$500–$6k at $100–$200/hr) while keeping quality.
gpt5_risks_types: Security, Privacy, Misinformation, Malicious actors and Misuse
gpt5_risks_justifications: This task can be safety-critical because performance changes at the code, CDN, or build-config layer can introduce subtle security/privacy regressions (e.g., mis-scoped caching or service-worker strategies that expose user data; loosening CSP for speed; disabling server-side validation; vulnerable bundling or dependency updates) and cause outages or revenue loss. LLMs increase risk via plausible but incorrect optimizations, hallucinated framework APIs, and recommending unvetted packages (supply-chain). When agentic, tool or CI/CD access can be abused to alter CI/CD, accept insecure diffs, or leak secrets via logs and environment variables; prompt-injection from perf reports or instrumented pages can coerce the agent to weaken CSP, widen cache keys, or embed third‑party trackers. Capability-induced oversight risk is significant because fluent explanations, synthetic benchmarks, and convincing diffs can cause developers to defer and skip deeper profiling or security review, letting subtle regressions ship.

Title: Web Developers
Task: Document technical factors such as server load, bandwidth, database performance, and browser and device types.
gpt5_rewards_justifications: High time savings from drafting standardized performance summaries, normalizing heterogeneous telemetry, generating compatibility matrices, and linking to dashboards. gpt5_risks_types: Security, Privacy, Misinformation
gpt5_risks_justifications: The task is generally not safety-critical; inaccuracies usually lead to wasted engineering time or suboptimal planning rather than direct harm. However, using LLMs raises security and privacy risk if sensitive telemetry or logs are shared (e.g., infrastructure topology, version numbers, internal URLs/IPs, cloud account IDs, API keys, or user PII). Agentic setups can be vulnerable to prompt injection from attacker-controlled log lines or web content, potentially causing data exfiltration or inclusion of risky details in docs. Capability-induced oversight risk exists: fluent summaries may cause developers to skip validating numbers, time windows, or units. Most errors are detectable by cross-checking dashboards and source logs, so residual risk is low-to-moderate if human review and data-handling controls are enforced.

Title: Web Developers
Task: Develop or implement procedures for ongoing Web site revision.
gpt5_rewards_justifications: High reward when used for drafting and scaffolding: generate change-management SOPs, RACI matrices, checklists, runbooks, release-note and PR templates, migration guides, maintenance-window comms, CI pipeline skeletons, CODEOWNERS, semantic-versioning configs, and monitoring/alerting templates; summarize repo history to propose revision cadences and dependency updates. With expert validation, dry runs, and security review, typical savings are 10–30 hours during initial procedure setup (approximately $600–$4,500 at $60–$150/hr) and 15–30 minutes per release for notes/checklists/comms (approximately $15–$75), often reducing cycle time by 20–40% while maintaining quality.
gpt5_risks_types: Security, Privacy, Misinformation, Malicious actors and Misuse, Discrimination
gpt5_risks_justifications: Safety-critical: procedures for ongoing site revision govern CI/CD, access, rollbacks, and content changes; errors can cause outages, data loss, or breaches. LLMs may produce persuasive but incomplete SOPs (e.g., missing separation of duties, approvals, secrets management, SBOM/dependency pinning, backup/restore/rollback drills, audit logging, canary/staged rollouts, WAF/CDN cache invalidation, and incident comms). Agentic use with repo/CI access is vulnerable to prompt-injection via code comments/markdown and can exfiltrate credentials or accept malicious PRs, creating supply-chain risk. Privacy risk arises if customer or config secrets are included in prompts or logs. Automation bias can lead teams to adopt flawed procedures with lighter review; subtle security/operational gaps may evade detection until production. Many issues are catchable with rigorous expert review, staging, and security sign-off, but the combination still elevates risk compared to human-only baselined processes.

Title: Web Developers
Task: Create Web models or prototypes that include physical, interface, logical, or data models.

With expert review using security/privacy/a11y checklists, type systems, OpenAPI validators, and a lightweight threat‑model pass, teams can maintain quality while reducing iteration loops. Typical savings: 20–40% on the modeling/prototyping phase of a small‑to‑mid feature (approximately 3–15 hours), and 10–25% on larger modules (approximately 10–30 hours). At $60–$140/hr this is roughly $180–$2,100 and $600–$4,200 per effort, respectively. Gains shrink for highly regulated flows where review dominates, but remain strong for documentation, variant exploration, and developer handoff.
gpt5_risks_types: Security, Privacy, Misinformation, Malicious actors and Misuse, Discrimination
gpt5_risks_justifications: Conditionally safety-critical: while prototypes/models aren’t production, their design choices (authN/Z, data flows, storage, third‑party dependencies, UX patterns) often propagate directly to shipped systems. LLMs can propose plausible but insecure architectures (e.g., storing JWTs in localStorage, weak CORS, missing CSRF, over‑broad scopes), leaky data models (excess PII, unclear retention), and incorrect compliance/accessibility claims (GDPR/WCAG/PCI) that are hard to spot later. Using real requirements or snippets in prompts can expose secrets/PII; agentic tools are vulnerable to prompt injection from specs or linked docs. Capability‑induced oversight risk is material: polished diagrams and narratives can cause teams to defer to LLM outputs and skip rigorous threat modeling, data‑minimization reviews, or A11y/security checklists; subtle authorization and multitenancy flaws may evade casual review. Misuse risk includes rapidly scaffolding deceptive UIs or phishing prototypes. Bias can enter via suggested default flows or labels that disadvantage groups. Most issues are catchable with disciplined design reviews, secure defaults, automated linters/scanners, and privacy/security sign‑off, but the combination of plausible narratives and subtle design errors keeps risk at a moderate level.

Title: Web Developers
Task: Provide clear, detailed descriptions of Web site specifications, such as product features, activities, software, communication protocols, programming languages, and operating systems software and hardware.
gpt5_rewards_justifications: High reward when positioned as a drafting and structuring assistant: generate spec templates, stakeholder-tailored versions, acceptance criteria, non-functional requirement checklists, traceability to user stories, and compatibility matrices, plus fast literature/standards triage—while experts verify technical claims. Typical savings are roughly 30–60% of drafting time on a 10–30 hour spec (about 3–15 hours), i.e., ~$300–$2,250 at ~$100–$150/hr, with quality maintained if teams enforce human-owned requirements, architecture/threat-model reviews, and source-verified references.
gpt5_risks_types: Misinformation, Security, Privacy
gpt5_risks_justifications: Safety-critical for organizations: inaccurate or incomplete specs can lead to insecure designs (e.g., permissive CORS, weak auth/session management, unsafe token/storage guidance), outages from wrong assumptions about protocols/compatibility, and compliance gaps. LLMs can hallucinate standards/limits, oversimplify browser/OS/network constraints, or omit edge cases. Their polished prose increases automation bias, reducing depth of architecture/threat-model reviews (capability-induced oversight risk). Tool-using agents can ingest poisoned or outdated docs (prompt/data injection), and sharing drafts with non-compliant services can leak proprietary or client data/PII. Many errors are catchable via senior review, checklists (e.g., OWASP ASVS), and testing, but subtle interoperability, performance, and security requirement omissions may evade early detection and surface late or in production.

Title: Web Developers
Task: Evaluate or recommend server hardware or software.

Typical savings are 20–40% of research/synthesis time (approximately 8–30 hours on a 40–80 hour evaluation; roughly $800– 6,000 at $100–$200/hr), plus faster stakeholder iteration and better documentation reuse. Savings shrink for niche/regulated stacks or when hands-on benchmarking dominates; maintain quality by requiring vendor-doc citations, reproducible comparisons, and pilot tests before purchase.
gpt5_risks_types: Security, Misinformation, Privacy, Malicious actors and Misuse
gpt5_risks_justifications: Safety-critical at the organizational level: incorrect server hardware/software choices can cause outages, security gaps, cost overruns, and compliance failures. LLM-specific risks include hallucinated specs or benchmarks, recommending outdated/EOL or unsupported components, misjudging compatibility (e.g., CPU instruction sets, kernel/driver, hypervisor, storage/NIC firmware), insecure-by-default configuration advice, and misleading TCO/license guidance. Capability-induced oversight risk is material: polished comparisons may lead experts to defer and skip independent verification, PoC testing, or vendor confirmation. If agents browse or ingest vendor pages, they can be prompt-injected or SEO-poisoned; using real infra details in prompts can leak sensitive topology, IPs, or credentials; recommending unvetted images or scripts introduces supply-chain risk. Compared with human-only review, LLM+expert workflows raise residual risk unless strict verification is enforced; with checklists, citations, and pilot tests, most errors are catchable, but subtle compatibility/security issues may still slip. Roughly a 10–30% higher chance of a poor recommendation under light oversight; near parity under rigorous controls.

Title: Web Developers
Task: Monitor security system performance logs to identify problems and notify security specialists when problems occur.
gpt5_rewards_justifications: Moderate reward if used for triage and summarization, not final judgment: cluster repetitive alerts, extract entities and timelines, correlate across sources, draft incident notes and notifications, and propose follow-up queries while analysts validate against SIEM rules and raw evidence. Typical savings: 20–40% faster triage on noisy days (approximately 0.5–2 analyst-hours/day, or $40–$300/day at $80–$150/hr), with reduced MTTA/MTTR, provided every alert rationale is traced to raw logs and model use is read-only, sandboxed, and privacy-compliant.
gpt5_risks_types: Security, Privacy, Misinformation, Malicious actors and Misuse
gpt5_risks_justifications: Safety-critical: missed or delayed detection of intrusions can cause material organizational harm. LLMs raise risk via false negatives (subtle IOCs or sequence-dependent anomalies missed), false positives that waste response bandwidth, overconfident but wrong causal narratives, and capability-induced oversight risk (fluent summaries cause analysts to review raw logs less carefully). Logs often contain attacker-controlled strings, enabling prompt injection to suppress or reframe alerts or leak secrets; if integrated with tools, an agent could be driven to unsafe actions. Using third-party LLMs can expose sensitive log/PII/credentials, creating privacy and breach risk. Compared to human-only workflows, LLM+human can increase residual miss/acceptance-of-bad-output risk materially (often 25–100% higher without strict controls; near-neutral with strong sandboxing, on-prem models, and mandatory evidence tracing), and failures are hard to detect under time pressure.

Title: Web Developers
Task: Install and configure hypertext transfer protocol (HTTP) servers and associated operating systems.
gpt5_rewards_justifications: LLMs can speed template creation (virtual hosts, reverse proxies, TLS, security headers), infra-as-code scaffolds (Ansible/Terraform), systemd units, cross-distro package/service commands, and log/error interpretation; they also draft runbooks and postmortems. With expert validation (config tests, scanners, CIS/OWASP checks, TLS/headers audits), typical savings are about 1–4 hours per server (approximately $75–$600 at $75–$150/hr). gpt5_risks_types: Security, Privacy, Misinformation, Malicious actors and Misuse
gpt5_risks_justifications: Safety-critical: HTTP server and OS misconfiguration can expose services, enable remote code execution, leak data/credentials, weaken TLS, disable logging/monitoring, or cause outages. LLMs frequently produce plausible but incorrect or outdated directives (e.g., mixing Nginx/Apache/Caddy syntax or distro/init differences), suggest insecure defaults (overly broad file permissions, open firewall rules, permissive CORS, weak TLS ciphers), or hallucinate modules/flags; many such issues are subtle and can pass smoke tests. High capability can induce deference—experts may copy/paste commands or configs and verify less thoroughly, increasing oversight risk. Agentic use with shell/SSH amplifies blast radius (e.g., running curl | bash, adding unvetted repos, opening ports). Privacy risk arises if keys, logs, or configs with PII/secret material are shared with non-compliant models. Prompt-injection via copied docs/snippets or error pages can steer unsafe actions. Net effect vs. human-only: higher likelihood of security-relevant misconfigurations unless rigorous hardening checklists, peer review, staging, and compliance controls are enforced.

Title: Web Developers
Task: Research, document, rate, or select alternatives for Web architecture or technologies.

LLMs can rapidly: enumerate candidate stacks, produce initial decision matrices, summarize official docs and changelogs, draft ADRs and RfPs, outline evaluation criteria and risk registers, generate vendor due‑diligence questions, estimate rough TCO scenarios from published pricing, and synthesize community signals into hypotheses to test. With a validation loop (check against primary docs, quick POCs, security/compliance review), teams often save roughly 20–50% of the upfront research and write‑up effort—about 5–20 hours on a typical 15–40 hour evaluation (approximately $500–$3,000 at $100–$150/hr)—while maintaining quality because critical facts and benchmarks are verified before a decision.
gpt5_risks_types: Misinformation, Security, Privacy, Malicious actors and Misuse
gpt5_risks_justifications: This task is safety-critical at the organizational level because architecture and technology choices directly affect security posture, data privacy/compliance, reliability, maintainability, and long‑term cost. LLMs raise risk by: (a) producing confident but outdated or incorrect comparisons, benchmarks, feature matrices, and license or SLA claims; (b) recommending immature, insecure, or poorly supported frameworks or services that later impose lock‑in or migration costs; (c) overlooking compliance or data‑residency constraints (e.g., PCI, HIPAA, GDPR) or misclassifying data flows; (d) underestimating non‑functional requirements such as scalability, latency, operability, or SLO/SLA implications; (e) misreading or misapplying open‑source licenses or cloud pricing, leading to hidden legal or TCO risk; (f) hallucinating references, adoption stats, or security postures; (g) being prompt‑injected when browsing or summarizing external docs, leading to biased or unsafe recommendations; (h) capability‑induced oversight risk: polished comparisons and confident rationale can cause architects to defer and skip independent benchmarks, threat models, or vendor verification; (i) privacy/security leakage if proprietary roadmaps, architectural diagrams, credentials, or client data are pasted into non‑compliant tools. These risks are partially mitigable if teams require primary‑source citations, run small POCs/benchmarks, perform formal threat modeling and license review, use enterprise‑grade LLMs with logging/guardrails, and separate discovery from decision authority with documented human sign‑off.

Title: Web Developers
Task: Develop system interaction or sequence diagrams.
gpt5_rewards_justifications: LLMs excel at turning requirements, tickets, or code into PlantUML/Mermaid, suggesting actors/messages, enumerating edge cases, and keeping docs in sync. With a human validating trust boundaries and security steps, teams can typically cut diagramming time by 30–60% for first drafts and 15–30% for updates, e.g., 0.5–3 hours saved per flow (approximately $25–$300 at $50–$100/hr). Gains come from rapid Mermaid/PlantUML generation, auto-enumeration of actors and messages, variant proposals, and keeping docs synced with code/comments. Equivalent quality is maintained when experts validate trust boundaries, authentication/authorization steps, error and retry paths, and data minimization against requirements and threat models, keep artifacts in version control, and use privacy-preserving or on-prem deployments for sensitive architectures.
gpt5_risks_types: Security, Privacy, Misinformation, Malicious actors and Misuse
gpt5_risks_justifications: Developing interaction/sequence diagrams is usually not safety-critical by itself, but incorrect or incomplete diagrams can propagate into insecure or faulty designs (e.g., missing auth/authorization checks, CSRF/nonce handling, token refresh, idempotency, error paths, or data minimization). Current LLMs produce fluent, authoritative diagrams that can look correct while omitting subtle trust boundaries; this can induce oversight/deference and let mistakes slip into design reviews. If external LLMs are used, prompts may expose internal architecture or sample payloads containing secrets/PII; agentic tooling can be prompt-injected by untrusted requirements or code comments. Most issues are catchable with expert review that traces each step to requirements and threat models and checks diagrams against code, so residual risk is generally low-to-moderate; however, for security- or compliance-critical flows the risk rises (≈3–4) without strict review.

Title: Web Developers
Task: Design and implement Web site security measures, such as firewalls and message encryption.

Gains come from: generating baseline secure configs (CSP, HSTS, CORS, TLS), IaC/WAF rule scaffolds, header sets, KMS/secret-rotation snippets, log/alert queries, threat-model and hardening checklists, and summarizing vendor or standards docs; plus drafting remediation plans and change documentation. With expert verification via linters and policy checks, SAST/DAST, TLS/header scanners, OWASP ASVS/CIS benchmarks, and peer review, teams can often reduce routine hardening/setup time by about 10–30% (e.g., 3–12 hours on a 20–40 hour effort), roughly $300–$1,800 at $100–$150/hr, while maintaining expert-level quality. For bespoke architectures or novel threats, verification dominates and savings drop to under 10%.
gpt5_risks_types: Security, Privacy, Misinformation, Malicious actors and Misuse
gpt5_risks_justifications: This is safety-critical: errors in firewall rules, TLS/cipher configuration, key management, CSP/CORS, auth (OAuth/OIDC), or encryption use can cause breaches, data loss, or regulatory exposure. LLMs raise risk via plausible but subtly wrong configs/code, outdated or hallucinated guidance, insecure crypto patterns (e.g., weak modes, poor RNG), recommending vulnerable dependencies, and agentic misconfigurations. Added risks: prompt injection through logs or user content influencing agents; inadvertent leakage of secrets in prompts; supply-chain insertion; integration security bugs. Relative to expert-only workflows, LLM+expert use can increase risk by introducing subtle but critical gaps (e.g., missing deny-all defaults, overly broad CORS, weak cipher suites) and by creating new attack surface in the model/agent. Quantitatively, compared to expert-only workflows, first-pass deployment risk of an exploitable misconfiguration can rise by roughly 15–40% if LLM outputs are not independently validated against authoritative hardening guides and automated checks. With strict controls (no secrets in prompts, read-only analysis sandboxes, pinned versions and SBOM review, policy-as-code and CI/CD guardrails, SAST/DAST, TLS and header scanners, canary releases, and mandatory expert sign-off), residual risk can be brought close to human-only baseline but rarely below it due to model/agent-specific vulnerabilities.

Title: Web Developers
Task: Incorporate technical considerations into Web site design plans, such as budgets, equipment, performance requirements, and legal issues including accessibility and privacy.
gpt5_rewards_justifications: Moderate reward if constrained to drafting and synthesis: generate requirements templates, WCAG checklists with test cases, DPIA/similar questionnaires, performance SLOs and budgets (with assumptions exposed), vendor comparison matrices, and stakeholder Q&A. gpt5_risks_justifications: This task is safety critical because advising on security mitigations and architectures influences the organization’s exposure to breaches, outages, regulatory penalties, and reputational harm. gpt5_risks_types: Security, Privacy, Misinformation, Malicious actors and Misuse
gpt5_risks_justifications: Safety-critical: yes. Pentest reports drive remediation priorities and executive risk decisions; incorrect severity, impact, or reproduction/remediation steps can leave critical issues unpatched or cause disruptive, unsafe changes. LLM-specific risks: (1) Misinformation—hallucinated evidence, wrong CVE/CWE/CVSS mapping, mis-stated business impact, or fabricated reproduction steps that look authoritative; (2) Security—processing hostile artifacts (burp exports, HTML, logs) can trigger prompt-injection or data-exfiltration via connected tools; using third-party LLMs expands the attack surface; (3) Privacy—client-confidential data/PII and sensitive network details may be retained or leaked if not handled in a compliant, isolated setup; (4) Misuse—overly detailed exploit narratives or PoCs, if leaked, can aid attackers; fluent but incorrect drafts can enable underqualified staff to produce convincing yet wrong reports. Capability-induced oversight risk: highly polished language and plausible justifications increase deference, so testers may skip verifying evidence chains, CVSS scoring, or environment-specific remediation—subtle errors can persist to sign-off. Compared to human-only documentation, LLM+human can raise the likelihood of undetected material errors and data handling failures by a meaningful margin (often one–two risk tiers higher) unless strong controls are in place (isolation, redaction, citation-to-evidence, two-person review, and prompt-injection defenses).
